newsitem.title: USA: Cordiant's Bates loses Miller in ad shift.
newsitem.headline: Cordiant's Bates loses Miller in ad shift.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc's Miller Brewing Co said it was reassigning the advertising for its two leading brands to new agencies, with Cordiant Plc's Bates USA unit hit hardest by the realignment.

Miller said it was moving its Miller Genuine Draft account, worth more than $50 million in estimated annual billings, from Bates to Portland, Ore.-based Wieden and Kennedy, best known for its Nike Inc advertising. It also said it would change its estimated $300 million in media buying and planning, long handled by Bates, to Chicago's Leo Burnett agency.
Miller also said it was shifting its Miller Lite beer, worth over $50 million in billings, to Fallon McElligott, of Minneapolis from Burnett.
Miller made the moves after watching market share decline for its flagship brands over the past year.

"These moves will help strengthen the brand-building communications of our two key premium brands and the effectiveness of our brand-building programs," said Neil Harrison, vice president of marketing.

It was the second time in two months that Burnett, the No. 2 U.S. agency brand in terms of billings revenue, lost a major account to its midwest rival, Fallon McElligott, which took the UAL Corp United Airlines account in a creative shootout in October. The blow for Burnett was softened, though, by the gain it made in acquiring all of Miller's media buying.
